claims.statement: The scheduler graph is a single-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered as the `scheduler` assistant in langgraph.json, and its `_launch` node deterministically routes one control tick without invoking an LLM.

The scheduler routes explicit tasks for reconciliation, baby-sit, expedited review, background tasks, workspace refresh, session cost, thread feedback, and agent cost; only a tick without a recognized task falls through to launch_scheduled_agent_run.
When a keyed scheduler tick is missing its required watch key, thread ID, or schedule ID, `_launch` returns a `missing_*` status result rather than raising.

Dashboard-managed recurring agent schedules normalize and validate a five-field cron expression, range-checking numeric values while supporting wildcards, ascending ranges, steps, and lists before storage.

A dashboard schedule Cron targets the scheduler with its schedule ID, and firing it creates a fresh durable agent thread/run while recording last thread, run, trigger time, or error in the separate `agent_schedule_run_state` namespace.

reconcile_stale_runs is the durable-dispatch safety net: it paginates busy threads, lists pending runs, and interrupts runs older than the default 1,800 seconds so a missed completion does not leave a thread busy indefinitely.
The reconcile sweep isolates per-thread errors and returns counts of checked threads, stale runs found, and cancelled runs.

Session-cost refresh is a self-terminating chain of stateless delayed scheduler runs: it updates the mapped Slack reply footer when cost becomes available, retries transient pending results through a fixed five-delay list, and clears the pending label on an unavailable or exhausted flow.

Each baby-sit watch is persisted in `baby_sit_watches` under a lower-cased owner/repo#PR key and binds the originating agent thread, head SHA/ref, GitHub App installation, captured run configuration, and SourceContext.

start_watch permits only one active agent thread per PR and ensures a single `*/10 * * * *` UTC baby-sit scheduler Cron by reusing a matching Cron or deleting duplicates; a brand-new watch row is rolled back if Cron creation fails.

The GitHub webhook route verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256`, routes CI events for an assigned and allowlisted repository to background processing, and baby-sit ignores non-failing payloads while matching active watches by head SHA or branch and deduplicating delivery IDs.

Both the webhook trigger and the Cron trigger serialize baby-sit evaluation with the same short-lived per-watch lock, so concurrent evaluation returns busy or is skipped rather than dispatching the same failure twice.

A baby-sit evaluation resets retry and dedupe state on a new head SHA; on a new failure fingerprint it enqueues a continuation run on the originating thread with a prompt that treats CI signals as untrusted, and removes the fingerprint again if dispatch fails.

Baby-sit considers CI successful only after the exact check-set fingerprint has remained unchanged for CHECK_SET_SETTLE_MINUTES (10 minutes), avoiding premature completion while checks are still being added.

Flaky reruns are capped at three per head SHA; record_retry enforces watch ownership and SHA consistency, increments durable retry state, and posts a source notification only once per head/check/safe GitHub URL.

Baby-sit stops watches for closure/merge, settled success, blocked checks, retry exhaustion, or three evaluation errors; it first tries the SourceContext Slack or GitHub destination and falls back to a queued terminal run on the originating agent thread.

The manage_baby_sit tool is the agent-facing surface for durable watches: it accepts canonical GitHub PR URLs, requires an executable thread, verifies an open PR and GitHub App installation on start, and enforces thread ownership for stop and retry recording.

Background-task monitoring is model-free: it maintains one every-minute thread-bound scheduler Cron, atomically claims each terminal sandbox task before enqueuing its notification, marks it delivered only after dispatch, and self-deletes monitor Crons after a locked recheck finds no running or pending task.

schedule_thread_wakeup creates a thread-bound, single-fire Cron directly against the `agent` assistant for delays from one minute through 24 hours, with an end time about 90 seconds after the UTC minute-rounded fire time and prepared run configuration.

Thread wakeups are limited to 10 between human messages, keyed to the latest human input-message generation; a new human message resets the budget whereas system messages do not, and the count is recorded before Cron creation.
Because fired wakeup Cron rows remain after their end time, schedule_thread_wakeup best-effort purges only expired `metadata.kind=thread_wakeup` rows, fully paginating before deletion.

Agent-usage cost refresh uses the scheduler's `agent_cost` task to retrieve a run-only LangSmith cost and persist it to the invocation usage record; retrieval or persistence failure advances through the fixed five-delay retry budget, while invalid or explicitly unavailable payloads terminate.

Focused tests cover scheduler routing, baby-sit lifecycle and deduplication, reconciliation failure isolation, bounded cost refreshes, and thread-wakeup validation, correlation, budgeting, concurrency, and cleanup.

Workspace refresh maintains a staggered daily scheduler Cron per workspace for full rebuilds, while stale snapshots can lazily enqueue an update refresh; full rebuilds run setup then update from a base snapshot and update refreshes run only the update script from the current snapshot.

A workspace refresh prevents overlapping work while a refresh is fresh, captures a snapshot only after every script succeeds, records failures while retaining the prior snapshot, and stops its throwaway builder sandbox in all outcomes.

Expedited review persists a separate approval lifecycle with a five-minute scheduler fallback Cron; evaluation retires approvals that are disabled, closed, superseded, or ineligible, while GitHub events provide immediate reevaluation.

Thread feedback uses delayed scheduler runs to wait for five quiet minutes, requeues itself if activity or a run delays the deadline, skips stale records under a thread lock, and marks the matching feedback event ready before optionally posting its Slack prompt.
